select
    cast(order_id as bigint) as order_id,
    cast(customer_id as varchar) as customer_id,
    cast(amount as double) as amount_usd,
    cast(currency as varchar) as currency,
    cast(status as varchar) as status,
    cast(created_at as timestamp) as created_at,
    cast(updated_at as timestamp) as updated_at,
    cast(created_at as date) as order_date
from "lab"."main"."orders"

select
    cast(customer_id as varchar) as customer_id,
    cast(country as varchar) as country,
    cast(tier as varchar) as tier,
    cast(is_active as boolean) as is_active,
    try_cast(
        nullif(trim(cast(valid_from as varchar)), '') as timestamp
    ) as valid_from,
    try_cast(
        nullif(trim(cast(valid_to as varchar)), '') as timestamp
    ) as valid_to
from "lab"."main"."customers"

with all_values as (

    select
        currency as value_field,
        count(*) as n_records

    from "lab"."main"."stg_orders"
    group by currency

)

select *
from all_values
where value_field not in (
    'USD','VND'
)

with all_values as (

    select
        status as value_field,
        count(*) as n_records

    from "lab"."main"."stg_orders"
    group by status

)

select *
from all_values
where value_field not in (
    'pending','completed','refunded','cancelled'
)

-- Test at fact-row granularity so positive orders cannot mask a negative order
-- after daily aggregation.
select
    order_id,
    customer_id,
    amount_usd,
    order_date
from "lab"."main"."stg_orders"
where status = 'completed'
  and amount_usd < 0

-- fct_daily_revenue is explicitly USD-denominated. Fail closed instead of
-- silently summing accepted VND values without a governed FX-rate source.
select *
from "lab"."main"."stg_orders"
where status = 'completed'
  and currency <> 'USD'

select amount_usd
from "lab"."main"."stg_orders"
where amount_usd is null

select order_id
from "lab"."main"."stg_orders"
where order_id is null

select
    order_id as unique_field,
    count(*) as n_records

from "lab"."main"."stg_orders"
where order_id is not null
group by order_id
having count(*) > 1

select customer_id
from "lab"."main"."stg_orders"
where customer_id is null

-- Active SCD records must be unique by customer. The mart is defensive against
-- duplicates, but this test still surfaces the upstream dimension defect.
select
    customer_id,
    count(*) as active_version_count
from "lab"."main"."stg_customers"
where is_active = true
group by customer_id
having count(*) > 1

select customer_id
from "lab"."main"."stg_customers"
where customer_id is null

select valid_from
from "lab"."main"."stg_customers"
where valid_from is null

select is_active
from "lab"."main"."stg_customers"
where is_active is null

), completed_orders as (
    select *
    from __dbt__cte__stg_orders
    where status = 'completed'
      and currency = 'USD'
),
ranked_active_customers as (
    select
        customer_id,
        row_number() over (
            partition by customer_id
            order by
                valid_from desc nulls last,
                country asc nulls last,
                tier asc nulls last,
                valid_to desc nulls last
        ) as active_version_rank
    from __dbt__cte__stg_customers
    where is_active = true
),
latest_active_customers as (
    -- Project only the key: one deterministic latest active row per customer is
    -- sufficient for this existence join and cannot multiply order facts.
    select customer_id
    from ranked_active_customers
    where active_version_rank = 1
)
select
    o.order_date,
    count(*) as completed_order_rows,
    sum(o.amount_usd) as daily_revenue
from completed_orders o
left join latest_active_customers c
    on o.customer_id = c.customer_id
group by 1
order by 1
